newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria condemns U.S. statement on Damascus blast.
newsitem.headline: Syria condemns U.S. statement on Damascus blast.

text.p: Syria on Friday rejected a U.S. warning against blaming Israel for a bomb blast in Damascus that killed nine people and wounded 44, saying it was "astonished" by the insensitivity of Washington's remarks.
A government spokesman said the statement by State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns lacked any sympathy with the families of the victims and disregarded feelings of Syrians.
"Syria was astonished by the statement of the spokesman of the State Department regarding the criminal act which left tens of civilians killed or wounded in Syria," the spokesman said in a statement.
He said the U.S. remarks "lacked any condemnation of the terrorist operation and did not have any human sympathy with families of the victims".

"With his statement, the U.S. spokesman gave the impression that his aim was to volunteer to relieve the one who is behind the terrorist action without taking into consideration feelings of the Syrian and Arab people," he said.

Burns said on Thursday the U.S. could not confirm a Syrian report that Israeli agents planted the bus bomb which exploded on Tuesday and warned Damascus against making "wild and irresponsible" statements without evidence.
A Syrian spokesman said in the first report about the explosion on Thursday that Israeli agents were behind the attack.

"The United States condemns this terrorist attack against innocent people. And there is every reason to believe that these were innocent people on that bus -- civilians who ought not have to fear for their lives when they travel around the city of Damascus," department spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

"And the United States extends our condolences to the families of the victims. The United States would have made this statement yesterday, had we known about the incident in any kind of detail," he said.

But on Syria's continued charges that Israel was responsible for the attack, Burns said: "It is not wise for any government to accuse another government of an act of terrorism without a foundation of evidence to support it. The United States is not aware of any evidence whatsoever that would link the Israeli government...to the bomb attack of a couple of days ago...or the other bombings in Damascus."
Syria earlier rejected an U.S. warning on Thursday against blaming Israel and said the previous U.S. statement lacked sympathy with the families of the victims and disregarded Syrians' feelings.
